title: 2013 was a tough time for Nintendo fans
description: Recently, Jack and Anni were at my place and I was playing music from Mario Kart World. Conversation drifted to one of Anni's favourite childhood games, New Super Mario Bros for the DS, and I offered them to play a game from the series together. I ended up booting up New Super Mario Bros. U for the Wii U, because I never got the port on the switch, which involved setting up the Wii U in front of my friends. I was suddenly transported back to Nintendo's flop era, around 2013, when this was the only game around the Wii U's launch.

Having to explain what the gamepad was, and that you need to use the gamepad to navigate the main menu, was almost embarrassing! I respect the gamepad - it walked so the switch could run - but it's so big and clunky, and I had to find the specific charger that it required (USB-C wasn't ubiquitous back then), just so I could start the game. Of course I also had to find batteries for the Wii Remotes I still had lying around, which was honestly quite enjoyable, although these controllers were janky and not working properly after all those years.

Then we went into the game itself, the original New Super Mario Bros. U, which bearing in mind is the fourth entry in a series of near-identical games. It was very much considered a safe Mario game that will sell well no matter what, so they barely changed it since the original DS title. And those game design decisions were plain to see. In this game, you can only save after beating a boss in a castle. If you die, you get kicked out of the level and have to re-enter, which takes almost a whole minute. There is pretty nifty multiplayer mechanic where if you die, you lose a life, but return as a bubble, so you can immediately keep playing. That's great, but you can also just bubble yourself with the press of the button, which means you can just coast through the levels, as long as the others keep playing. Also, Jack lost all their lives and simply had to watch Anni and me play without them! These things are all pretty inconceivable today.

Vibes-wise, I actually like the Wii U, and I think the soundtracks of even generic games like New Super Mario Bros. U are pretty solid. However, it's unforgivable that you can't play as Peach. Back then Nintendo didn't believe in women. The hardest part about that era though was just the absolute dearth of games! Nowadays we are spoiled by a rich and successful Nintendo releasing 1st party games every month. Back then we waited half a year for Pikmin 3 or Splatoon or Yoshi's Woolly World or something. It was slim pickings. Only until 2017's Breath of the Wild did it all start coming together for Nintendo and for us, the die-hard Nintendo fans.

Otherwise my life has been a constant stream of activity, and I'm starved for days off. I've always been like this and I don't see it changing anytime soon. At some point my body will say no and make me ill, but until then I'm saying yes to all plans because FOMO is too strong. And in website news, I've made two more playlists for your (and my own) enjoyment. First is very sad music for when you feel miserable and you want to lean into the bad feelings, and the second is for when the wind is coursing through your hair while you are cycling down a hill or something.

entries.title: Star Fox
description: I have fond memories of the original game, playing it over and over just on the easy route because I was a dumb child, and having my mind blown when you can do the 'harder' route for an alternate ending. I decided to try the remake because the vibes looked good. I saw some gameplay of the meteorite belt and thought it looked gorgeous, and it is! But if I'm honest, I wasn't totally blown away. I think it's a lot to do with the fact that the game is on rails and you're not free to just fly around and explore.

I decided while I was playing it that maybe these rail shooter games aren't for me. I already know I'm not into first person shooters, and this isn't so different, although I like the arcade flair of this game. I don't feel inspired to go back through the levels and do them more efficiently or beat the challenges, but I guess that's OK, it's just not for me. I also tried out the multiplayer but it was too stressful, and I really don't enjoy team games.

The character designs are fine, shocking on first viewing but you get used to them very quickly. Although Falco is at his most ugly here. At first I was horrified but I remembered that Falco has always been ugly, so making him so deeply ugly here is only appropriate.

Finally, I feel like the soundtrack is too generic-orchestra. I would have preferred something weird and remarkable. The original tracks are pretty nice and there was a lot of potential there, but with the exception of maybe Zoness, the new music didn't really hit for me. Also, I thought the ending sequence with James totally ridiculous. I really feel like they fucked that up! All emotional weight gone. And the ending scene where all the animals are just running, ridiculous.

entries.title: So Help Me God
description: This album inspired me to make my 'wind through your hair' mix because these string arrangements make me feel like I'm cycling home on a warm summer's evening. It's just such a lush album. I adore the way the tempo slows down in 'Comfort', it makes it feel like you're opening the window in the morning. 'American Sonnet' is also a wild track. Those eerie, distant-sounding horn stabs, really ominous. The ending of the song as well.
entries.metadata: Artist: Kelsey Lu, Release: 2026, for a list of favourite tracks, please visit the albums page!

entries.title: Wind Through Your Hair
description: There's nothing better than being in a good mood while the weather is good, you are travelling and the wind is flowing through your hair. In German they call it Fahrtwind. With this playlist, I'm trying to capture that vibe of cycling on a warm summer evening, or driving with the top down. We've got string sections to the max here and we are reconnecting with the element of Air.
entries.metadata: For the tracklist, visit the playlists page!

entries.title: Lean Into The Sadness
description: I'm someone whose mood is very much affected by the music I'm listening. Sometimes when I'm upset, I can listen to happier, uplifting music and it eventually gets me out of the dumps. Sometimes though, all I want to do is lean into my sadness and indulge myself to the max in my feelings. This playlist is for moments like those. And just remember: it's OK to cry - you will feel better afterwards.
entries.metadata: For the tracklist, visit the playlists page!

entries.title: SimCity
description: I was totally caught off guard by this release, because I knew next to nothing about this game. Originally publishing for the SNES, this development studio went on to create a spin-off of this series called 'The Sims' after it was bought by EA. But before this, the world was treated to this RTS gem with excellent vibes.

The vibes of this soundtrack are truly off the charts! I never would have guessed. Listening to it, I thought to myself that it has strong Pilotwings vibes, and lo and behold, the composer Soyo Oka - she's the composer for Pilotwings! Also, she did Super Mario Kart, which makes so much sense. The music is spacey, almost jazzy, and has some nice classical influences.

The game features a different track depending on how big your city is, and the largest size, Megalopolis, has music that made me stop what I was doing and listen to it again. What a cool, proggy ending before the loop goes round. Super nice sounding. It really makes me want to play the game.
entries.metadata: Platform: SNES, for a list of favourite tracks, please visit the nintendo soundtracks page!

entries.title: Super Mario Sunshine
description: Such a classic soundtrack! I've always loved this game for commiting to making the whole thing take place on a beautiful island. Each part of the island has its own vibe but is also part of the connected whole. You've got latin rhythms behind all these tracks and I just live for that shit. It starts straight away with the low-key great remix of the underground theme in Delfino Airstrip, with a nice slow cha-cha rhythm.

Personal highlights for me are definitely Gelato Beach (maximum vibes), Pinna Park (love to play it on the piano), Sirena Beach (actually kinda creepy), and Pianta Village (party music for a party town). Also special shoutouts to the casino music that they ended up using for all those minigames in the DS era. It's so good.
entries.metadata: Platform: Gamecube, for a list of favourite tracks, please visit the nintendo soundtracks page!

entries.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave
description: These tracks are great and I'm really looking forward to this game! The fire emblem team have been killing it ever since Awakening so I just know we're in for another banger soundtrack again this time round. Sign me up! I think I'm gonna play as the Alucard-like guy because he seems very extra.
entries.metadata: Platform: Switch 2, for a list of favourite tracks, please visit the nintendo soundtracks page!

entries.title: Virtual Boy Wario Land
description: I feel like all these tracks were designed to sound weird and uncomfortable. But then again Wario Land music was always bad (until the legendary Wario Land 4). One track 'Stage BGM 7' is kinda cool because it riffs on Ravel's Bolero.
entries.metadata: Platform: Virtual Boy, for a list of favourite tracks, please visit the nintendo soundtracks page!

entries.title: Mario Clash
description: Wow this soundtrack really is a write off. Really bad. Nothing salvageable here.
entries.metadata: Platform: Virtual Boy, for a list of favourite tracks, please visit the nintendo soundtracks page!

entries.title: Galactic Pinball
description: Oh DAMN! After listening to all these other pretty shit virtual boy soundtracks, I was suddenly blown away by this one! The compositions are so ambitious and full of fun harmonies. It sounds super sci-fi and I'm obsessed. The title screen music alone is crazy enough but then you have the ominous sounding 'Colony', the 'UFO (Lucky Star)' track which is half Rainbow Road and half Kirby Rainbow Resort. So fun. Highly recommend.
entries.metadata: Platform: Virtual Boy, for a list of favourite tracks, please visit the nintendo soundtracks page!

entries.title: Teleroboxer
description: This punch out clone is going for rock music which I think sounds shit on this soundfont. I like the disco song, and the needlessly epic music for your records. They didn't need to go that hard for that.
entries.metadata: Platform: Virtual Boy, for a list of favourite tracks, please visit the nintendo soundtracks page!

entries.title: Mario's Tennis
description: This soundtrack is alright, it could be a lot worse. I don't appreciate that each song loops like 4 times, but there are a couple of nice tracks in here.
